newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German food sales in west still low-poll.
newsitem.headline: East German food sales in west still low-poll.

text.p: Western Germany is still buying hardly any food from the eastern states, the BVS German privatisation agency said on Thursday.

Chairman of the BVS advisory board Klaus von Dohnanyi said that, seven years after German unification, east German firms represented only one percent of the retail food sales in the western part of the country.

"Only the federal government has succeeded in implementing the 15 to 20 percent market share goals (for purchases from east German firms)." Dohnanyi said, speaking at the Marketing Services Fair in Frankfurt. "But even there growth is slowing."

A poll of 60 west German public institutions ordered by the BVS and carried out by the Sinus research institute found that less than one percent of states' and cities' food purchases are of eastern German products.

"Companies in east Germany have to get used to the fact that they can no longer expect preference from government institutions simply because they come from east Germany," said Sinus director Werner Soergel.
